abstract.text: Neural network based word embeddings, such as Word2Vec and GloVe, are purely data driven in that they capture the distributional information about words from the training corpus. Past works have attempted to improve these embeddings by incorporating semantic knowledge from lexical resources like WordNet. Some techniques like retrofitting modify word embeddings in the post-processing stage while some others use a joint learning approach by modifying the objective function of neural networks. In this paper, we discuss two novel approaches for incorporating semantic knowledge into word embeddings. In the first approach, we take advantage of Levy et al’s work which showed that using SVD based methods on co-occurrence matrix provide similar performance to neural network based embeddings. We propose a sprinkling technique to add semantic relations to the co-occurrence matrix directly before factorization. In the second approach, WordNet similarity scores are used to improve the retrofitting method. We evaluate the proposed methods in both intrinsic and extrinsic tasks and observe significant improvements over the baselines in many of the datasets.

thesis.text: Injecting lexical knowledge into word embeddings via sprinkling into the SPPMI matrix and via WordNet-similarity-weighted retrofitting improves their quality on word similarity, analogy, NER, and POS tasks.

sections.summary: Introduces the paper's motivation: purely distributional embeddings can be improved with lexical knowledge. Reviews prediction-based and count-based embeddings, post-processing methods such as retrofitting and counterfitting, joint-learning methods, and the sprinkling/LSI idea that motivates the two proposed approaches.
sections.title: Motivation and Related Work

sections.summary: Presents the two core methods. SS-PPMI and DSS-PPMI modify the shifted PPMI matrix by concatenating one or multiple hop-limited reachability matrices from WordNet or PPDB before SVD. W-Retrofitting replaces degree-based weights in retrofitting with normalized WordNet similarity scores, using max synset similarity and multi-hop neighbours.
sections.title: Proposed Models: Sprinkling and Weighted Retrofitting

sections.summary: Describes the intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation setup. Intrinsic tasks include word similarity datasets (MEN, MTurk, RG65, RW, SimLex999, TR9856, WS353 variants) and analogy datasets (Google, MSR, SemEval2012). Extrinsic tasks are POS tagging and NER. Knowledge sources are WordNet and PPDB; SPPMI is built from a Wikipedia dump. Baselines include GloVe, retrofitting, SPPMI, and SynGCN.
sections.title: Experimental Setup

sections.summary: Reports that reachability matrices alone capture similarity but not relatedness. SS-PPMI and DSS-PPMI improve word similarity and analogy, especially on SimLex999, RG65, and WS353. Double sprinkling and more hops generally help similarity, with marginal gains on relatedness and analogy.
sections.title: Sprinkling Results

source_span.end_text: as shown by the results in Table 9.

sections.summary: Evaluates W-Retrofitting on GloVe and SPPMI vectors. Using PPDB with inverse path similarity and WordNet with Jiang-Conrath weights, it outperforms retrofitting on many similarity benchmarks and remains competitive on analogy. Overall, sprinkling gives the best balance of similarity and relatedness. On extrinsic POS and NER, W-Retrofitting is comparable to SynGCN.
sections.title: W-Retrofitting and Overall/Extrinsic Results

sections.summary: Recaps the two approaches and their improvements across similarity, analogy, and extrinsic tasks. Future directions include weighting relations in the reachability matrix with WordNet or co-occurrence information, using adaptive sprinkling, and initializing contextual pretrained models with these embeddings.
sections.title: Conclusion and Future Work
